The combined financial toll of Trump's war in Iran has imposed new tradeoffs on the federal budget and increased prices for millions of American consumers. 

Join us on Thursday, April 2, for an online discussion with @econJaredB, Catherine Wolfram, and moderator @AndrwPMiller on the economic costs of the war. americanprogress.org/events/…

President Trump has now spent more than $25 billion on his reckless war in Iran—that's BILLIONS that could feed, house, and care for families here at home.

Video

In a new attack on clean energy and abuse of taxpayer dollars, the Trump administration will pay TotalEnergies nearly $1 billion to cancel two offshore wind projects that would have powered 1.3 million homes in New Jersey and North Carolina. ampr.gs/4s1vNAv

Americans are paying for Trump's reckless and immoral war in Iran.


The New York Times (@nytimes)

Breaking news: The average price of gasoline in the U.S. is now more than $4 a gallon, the first time it has reached that level since 2022.

nyti.ms/4m6Ri1M

The war in Iran has already cost the American taxpayer over $25 billion. More than 3 million people could be housed in Section 8 for a year with that amount.
This past weekend's “No Kings’’ protests dominated the public narrative and focused the nation’s attention on the need for transformative, pro-democracy changes from the government. ampr.gs/4tn2RUZ
We've already spent over $25 billion on Trump's war in Iran. That money could have provided child care to 1.8 million children for a year.

Across 3,300 cities and towns, an estimated 8 million Americans gathered at a No Kings rally to protest the Trump administration's authoritarian policies, marking steady progress toward the 3.5% of the population needed to force the government's hand. ampr.gs/4tn2RUZ
CAP's state-by-state analysis finds that the Trump administration’s trade policies are a hefty tax on small businesses, the backbone of America’s workforce. americanprogress.org/article…
